title: Proteomics and machine learning nominate PYGB to separate inverted urothelial papilloma
summary: Mass-spectrometry proteomics of inverted urothelial papilloma, papillary urothelial carcinoma and normal urothelium, followed by machine-learning analysis, shortlisted SERPINH1, PKP2 and PYGB. Immunohistochemistry in an independent sample cohort confirmed PYGB as a marker distinguishing inverted urothelial papilloma from papillary urothelial carcinoma with inverted growth. The machine-learning algorithm is not named in the abstract and cohort sizes were not seen.
ai_technology: Mass-spectrometry proteomics with machine-learning shortlisting of candidate proteins (SERPINH1, PKP2, PYGB)
organization: Seoul National University College of Medicine; Severance Hospital, Yonsei University College of Medicine

evidence.tested: Immunohistochemical validation of the shortlisted PYGB marker in an independent sample cohort.
evidence.unknown: The specific machine-learning algorithm, cohort sizes and diagnostic accuracy; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Machine learning shortlisted candidate protein biomarkers from the proteomic data.
